svg.title: effort-router: how a message is routed to chat, design or impl
svg.desc: A railway diagram. A message enters from the left. Slash commands, notifications and empty prompts leave on a spur, untouched. A pinned mode or a bare approval while in impl takes a bypass straight to the switch, with no classifier call. Any other message stops at the classifier, a haiku model at low effort that answers in a few seconds with chat, design or impl and a confidence; at 0.6 or more it throws the switch. An answer below 0.6, a timeout after 6 seconds or a failure leaves the switch where it was, and a new session starts set to impl. The chat line runs the main loop at low effort. The design line, straight on from the switch, runs it at xhigh effort, with no hand-off. The impl line runs it at high effort as an orchestrator, which hands the change to an implementer agent on opus at high effort down a siding and reviews it when it comes back. A board at the bottom shows the band above the prompt: the mode, the model and effort the main loop ran with, and how the last message was routed.
svg.text: Every message you send runs on one of three lines, and the line sets the effort of the main loop.

The main loop keeps its model, main_model: only its effort changes, unless you raised it past high. Other subagents keep their own model and effort.
